claims.supporting_quote: Without a bank account, workers cannot contribute and profit from the existing centralized micro task marketplace.

claims.claim: Signup and approval processes in centralized micro task systems are invasive, privacy challenging, time consuming, and unclear, and they function as market entry barriers for micro task workers.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: centralized micro task systems
claims.supporting_quote: Finally, micro workers in centralized systems are faced with invasive, privacy challenging, time consuming, and unclear signup and approval processes that create market entry barriers for micro task workers.

claims.claim: Decentralized crypto market solutions can significantly optimize the existing mechanical turk market while simultaneously democratizing access to it.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: mechanical turk and micro task markets
claims.supporting_quote: Decentralized crypto market solutions for the existing mechanical turk market can provide significant optimization while democratizing market access.

claims.claim: Semada is stipulated as an autonomous, decentralized, open source protocol on the Ethereum blockchain that enables domain specific reputation verification for human task crowdsourcing.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
claims.supporting_quote: Semada is an autonomous, decentralized, open-source protocol29 that enables domain specific reputation verification for human task crowdsourcing, built on the ETHEREUM blockchain.

claims.claim: The protocol lowers cost because it removes the manual verification step and the associated multiplication of micro task work that centralized systems require, letting decentralized workers capture the gains from disintermediation.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: micro task crowdsourcing under the Semada Protocol
claims.supporting_quote: the Semada Protocol removes the manual verification and the associated multiplication of micro task work necessitated by centralized systems, enabling its decentralized micro task workers to profit from the disintermediation.

claims.claim: Reputation tokens supply a staking mechanism that incentivizes high quality work and task completion by workers, and that simultaneously lets requesters verify and track worker quality, integrity, and quantity.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: participants staking reputation tokens on the platform
claims.supporting_quote: Through the reputation tokens, the Semada Protocol provides a micro task worker reputation staking mechanism that incentivizes high quality work and task completion by workers.

claims.claim: Unlike its decentralized competitors, the Semada Protocol is claimed to be resistant to both Sybil attacks and Tyranny of the Majority attacks.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: comparison with existing decentralized mechanical turk protocols
claims.supporting_quote: However, unlike its decentralized competitors, the Semada Protocol ensures Sybil Attack and Tyranny of the Majority attack resistance.

claims.claim: The protocol architecture together with its incentive structure is what produces enhanced 51 percent attack resistance, which the author claims exceeds prior reputation verification attempts in both decentralized and centralized networks.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: reputation verification networks
claims.supporting_quote: The Semada Protocol architecture and its incentive structure facilitates enhanced 51% attack resistance unlike any previous reputation verification attempts in decentralized and centralized networks.

claims.claim: Because platform access requires only an internet connection rather than a bank account, the decentralized design expands the micro task labor pool by up to 40 percent, including the unbanked.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: workers with internet access
including unbanked workers
claims.supporting_quote: The Semada Platform GUI gives access to anyone with an internet connection, including the unbanked. Thus, expanding the micro task labor pool by up to 40%.

claims.claim: A key design goal is a minimal and robust architecture, because minimality is what permits later construction of more complex automated validation logic and machine expert validators.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: architecture of the validation platform
claims.supporting_quote: A key design goal of Semada is to create a minimal and robust architecture that allows for creating much more complex and automated validation logic, as well as machine expert validators.

claims.claim: Validation experts could evolve from humans into smart contracts, which would allow validation itself to become automated.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: future development of the platform
claims.supporting_quote: For instance, experts could evolve from humans to smart contracts in order to allow for the automation of validation.

claims.claim: Rather than repeating the same task across many workers to reach quality, the architecture verifies quality directly by examining and validating individual worker task performance through reputation verification.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: micro tasks routed through the reputation verification architecture
claims.supporting_quote: Instead of repeating work on given tasks to attain high quality work products for micro tasks, Semada uses an architecture of reputation verification that examines micro worker task performance and verifies the validity and quality of the work.

claims.claim: Staking creates disincentives for malicious actors, and it is this disincentive structure that makes the network both more efficient and attack resistant.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: workers and verifiers who have reputation tokens at stake
claims.supporting_quote: Semada staking mechanism creates disincentives for malicious actors, enhancing the efficiency of the Semada Network and making it attack resistant.

claims.claim: Verifiers stake proportionally smaller amounts of reputation tokens than workers, because their higher reputation scores make them less likely to be malicious actors.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: verifiers with higher reputation scores than the workers they verify
claims.supporting_quote: Similarly, verifiers stake (a proportionally smaller) amount of reputation tokens because verifiers have a higher reputation score and are therefore less likely to be malicious actors.

claims.claim: Reputation scores clear the market on both sides: a low requester score makes workers less likely to accept that requester's offers, and a low worker score reduces the worker's likelihood of retention.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: two sided reputation scoring visible to both parties
claims.supporting_quote: If requesters have a lower reputation score, workers become less likely to accept requesters' offers. In turn, low reputation scores for micro task workers result in a lower likelihood of retention for micro task work on the Semada Network.

claims.claim: Because requesters select workers by reputation score, workers acquire an incentive to keep their scores high by performing tasks with high accuracy and efficiency.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: requesters can observe and select on reputation score
claims.supporting_quote: Requesters can select workers based on their reputation score, giving workers an incentive to keep the reputation scores high by performing micro tasks with high accuracy and efficiency.

claims.claim: The reputation score mechanism serves a discriminating function, separating malicious actors from simple mistakes and protecting workers and verifiers against fraudulent requesters and badly designed requests.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
claims.supporting_quote: The reputation score mechanism helps discern malicious actors and simple mistakes. It also protects workers and verifiers from fraudulent requesters and suboptimally designed requests.

claims.claim: Sharing all work fees with the expertise creates a positive feedback loop: the more fees flow to the platform, the more reputation is worth, and the more workers prefer reputation tokens to one time fees.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: protocol enforces that users seeking validation send all work fees to the platform
claims.supporting_quote: Choosing to enforce a protocol where all fees are shared with the expertise creates a successful positive feedback loop: The more fees are sent to the platform, the more the reputation is worth; which means the reputation tokens will be more desirable to workers than one-time fees.

claims.claim: Once participants are vested through reputation, they police the system themselves, which raises security, which in turn attracts more public fees and closes the loop.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: constituents hold vested reputation stakes
claims.supporting_quote: This in turn means the system will be carefully policed by vested constituents. This makes the system more secure; so the platform will attract more public fees.

claims.claim: The payment design allows secure off chain payments without gas consumption, with settlement transferred onto the Ethereum blockchain at a later date, which the author claims is superior to the payment channel approach used by decentralized competitors.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: payments among requesters, workers, and verifiers
claims.supporting_quote: It allows for secure off chain payments without using gas before transferring those payments on the ETHEREUM blockchain at a later date.

claims.claim: The gamification design borrows the foundational proof of work principle that verifying a game was played properly is far easier than playing it properly, which is why bench validators can check task performance almost fully automatically.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: tasks structured as games with forum defined rules and rewards
claims.supporting_quote: The foundational principle of proof of work in the blockchain suggests that it is a lot easier to verify a game was played properly than it is to play it properly.

claims.claim: Gamification is stipulated as the process of adding games or game like elements, such as a micro task, in order to encourage active worker participation, boost motivation, and increase user loyalty.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
claims.supporting_quote: Gamification is defined as the process of adding games or game-like elements, such as a micro-task, to encourage active task worker participation, boost motivation, and increase user loyalty.

claims.claim: Existing decentralized gamification attempts for micro task workers fail because they are monodimensional and permit earning only by playing the game, whereas a multidimensional design gives players several ways to earn and builds stronger loyalty.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: decentralized micro task platforms using gamification
claims.supporting_quote: Unlike other decentralized gamification attempts for micro task workers that are monodimensional and only allow earning by playing the game, the Semada platform offers players multiple opportunities to earn by playing.

claims.claim: Centralized mechanical turk marketplace leaders operate as rent seeking intermediaries that generate numerous inefficiencies in the market and deprive freelance workers of a share in the profits the platforms capture.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: centralized micro task marketplaces including MTurk and Crowdflower
claims.supporting_quote: Similarly, centralized mechanical turk marketplace leaders act as rent seeking intermediaries that create numerous inefficiencies in the market.

claims.claim: Centralized industry leaders in the freelancer market, including Upwork, Amazon, and Fiverr, charge up to 40 percent in transaction fees.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: centralized freelance marketplaces as of 2018
claims.supporting_quote: Centralized industry leaders in the freelancer market, including Upwork, Amazon, and Fiverr charge up to 40% in transaction fees.

claims.claim: Attack resistance should be designed to increase as the platform grows, in contrast to designs like GEMS that detect and ban malicious actors, because a self enforcement mechanism lets the incentive system steer users away from bad actors once the system matures.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: after the system reaches maturity
claims.supporting_quote: Unlike GEMS, which bans malicious actors detected through the GEMS trust mechanism from the platform, the Semada platform has a self-enforcement mechanism.

claims.claim: Centralized platform fees charged to requesters for the right to submit tasks exert downward pressure on worker compensation, so the fee structure itself is what depresses pay.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: centralized marketplaces such as Crowdflower and MTurk
claims.supporting_quote: Such centralized fees add downward pressure on the platforms' worker compensation.

claims.claim: Removing centralized fees produces a more efficient marketplace for workers, verifiers, and requesters alike by eliminating rent seeking intermediaries, leaving gas for posters as the only cost.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: posters pay gas on the Ethereum blockchain, viewers do not
claims.supporting_quote: The lack of fees on the Semada platform creates a more efficient marketplace for workers, verifiers, and requesters alike through the removal of the rent seeking intermediators.

claims.claim: Payment intermediary fees such as Paypal's are viable only for higher volume workers who can eventually avoid them, so they operate as an entry barrier against new micro task workers.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: centralized platforms relying on third party payment intermediaries
claims.supporting_quote: The fees make is only economically viable for higher volume workers who can at some point avoid the Paypal fees but create barriers to entry for new micro task workers.

claims.claim: Because holding and storing the platform's tokens requires no banking relationship, internet access is the only requirement for a micro task worker to earn a living on the platform.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: payment entirely in crypto tokens
requesters post ETH to request task completion
claims.supporting_quote: Holding and storing Semada tokens does not necessitate a banking relationship. All that is needed for a micro task worker to earn a living on the Semada Platform is access to the Internet.

claims.claim: Poor user interface quality on centralized micro task platforms increases both the time workers need per task and their error rate, and both effects lower worker earning ability.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: centralized micro task platforms with outdated interfaces
claims.supporting_quote: The lacking quality in mechanical turk user interfaces also significantly increases the time for workers to perform tasks and increases the error rate in performing tasks both of which significantly lower worker earning ability on such platforms.

claims.claim: Building interface modules as reusable open source components lets future requesters build new modules on existing ones, which generates network effects within the platform.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: modules built on top of the platform as open source
claims.supporting_quote: All open source software components of modules are reusable and enable future requesters to build new modules on existing ones, enabling superior network effects within the Semada Platform.

claims.claim: Centralized approval processes and identity requirements for worker registration significantly limit the registration of new micro task workers.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: centralized micro task platforms requiring identity verified registration
claims.supporting_quote: According to a study by the World Bank, centralized approval processes and identity requirements for mechanical turk worker registration creates significant limitations for the registration of new workers for micro task platforms.

claims.claim: Centralized platforms cannot simply drop identity verification, because they need it to keep malicious actors from abusing the network and to ensure work quality; this is the tradeoff a staking based design is meant to dissolve.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: centralized micro task platforms
claims.supporting_quote: However, centralized micro task platforms need to verify identity to prevent malicious actors from abusing the network and ensure work quality.

claims.claim: Because the reputation token staking mechanism supplies attack resistance directly, users need not verify their identity to complete micro tasks, which circumvents the costs, delays, and privacy surrender attached to centralized identity verification and thereby enlarges the willing labor pool.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: workers staking reputation tokens rather than proving identity
claims.supporting_quote: By contrast, on the Semada Platform, users do not need to verify their identity to complete micro tasks. The Semada Protocol architecture, and specifically its reputation token staking mechanism, make the Semada Platform attack resistant.

claims.claim: Mechanical turk is only one application of the underlying reputation protocol, and further use cases that cannot presently be conceptualized will emerge over time.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: future evolution of the protocol ecosystem
claims.supporting_quote: Other use cases will evolve on the Semada Platform over time and applications for the Semada Protocol that cannot currently be conceptualized will materialize.

claims.claim: Initial Coin Offerings provide unprecedented liquidity and efficiency for capital formation while minimizing transaction cost.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
claims.supporting_quote: Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs) provide unprecedented liquidity and efficiency for capital formation while minimizing transaction cost.

claims.claim: Unlike other means of capital formation, ICOs allow promoters to raise funds without sacrificing equity, so proceeds can be used exclusively for product development.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
claims.supporting_quote: Unlike other means of capital formation, ICO's allow promoters to avoid sacrificing equity for financing. Instead, ICO promoters can use the proceeds of the ICO exclusively for product development.

claims.claim: ICOs lower barriers to entry for a diverse body of investors and thereby increase the diversity and heterogeneity of start-up funding.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
claims.supporting_quote: ICOs provide low barriers to entry for a diverse body of investors and thus increase the diversity and the heterogeneity of start-up funding.

claims.claim: ICOs enable borderless online sales with fewer points of friction, letting promoters bypass typical legal, jurisdictional, and business hurdles by marketing directly to a worldwide investor pool.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
claims.supporting_quote: First, ICOs enable borderless online sales with much fewer points of friction. ICOs enable the promoters to bypass the typical legal, jurisdictional, and business hurdles by directly marketing to a worldwide pool of investors.

claims.claim: Unlike shareholders in traditional corporate structures who can vote for or nominate directors, ICO investors have no control whatsoever over promoters.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
claims.supporting_quote: Unlike shareholders in the traditional corporate infrastructure who are able vote for or against directors or to nominate directors, ICO investors have not control over the promoters whatsoever.

claims.claim: Capped ICO raises, adopted to address investor uncertainty about platform valuation in uncapped raises, backfire by creating strong incentives for investors to get in first and thereby raising the likelihood of retail investor frenzy.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: capped ICO raises
claims.supporting_quote: However, capped ICO raises crate significant incentive for investors to attempt to get in first, raising the likelihood of retail investor frenzy.

claims.claim: The absence of mandatory disclosure requirements for ICOs leads many promoters to make irregular or no disclosures about the platform over time, producing a significant lack of transparency in the ICO market.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
claims.supporting_quote: Moreover, the lack of mandatory disclosures for ICOs leads many promoters to make irregular or no disclosures about the platform as time passes, leading to a significant lack of transparency in the ICO market.

claims.claim: ICO promoters can alter the smart contract to change the sales rules mid-course during the ICO.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
claims.supporting_quote: Promoters can also change the smart contract to change ICO sales rules mid-course during the ICO.

claims.claim: Because crypto platforms have no product and no revenue to offset costs, the funds they raise must typically last for the entire lifecycle of the platform, forcing them to set aside a large number of tokens for future funding needs.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: crypto platforms without revenue-generating products
claims.supporting_quote: because they have no product and no revenue to offset costs, crypto platforms' revenue raised is typically required to last for the lifecycle of the platform, requiring crypto platforms to set aside a large number of tokens for future funding needs.

claims.claim: ICO investors have no preemptive rights or other anti-dilution protections, so they may be diluted if promoters later issue more reserve tokens to additional investors.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
claims.supporting_quote: ICO investors have no preemptive rights or other anti- dilution protections. If the promoters decide to issue more reserve tokens to additional investors, the ICO investors may be diluted in the future.

claims.claim: Because ICOs give investors very limited assurances through upfront and continuous disclosures, the token market is highly volatile.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
claims.supporting_quote: ICOs on the other hand, give investors very limited assurances through upfront and continuous disclosures, making the token market highly volatile.

claims.claim: Token holders typically receive no liquidity preference protecting them if the platform they invested in goes bankrupt or terminates.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
claims.supporting_quote: Token holders typically do not receive a liquidity preference that would protect them in the case of bankruptcy or termination of the platform they invested in.

claims.claim: The top 25 ICO jurisdictions in this study are identified from ICO WatchList data, which ranks countries by the number of ICOs launched and reports how much was raised through those ICO projects.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: top 25 ICO countries
ICO WatchList as the underlying data source
claims.supporting_quote: To determine the ICO's used for this project, the author used data generated by ICO WatchList.1 ICO WatchList ranks countries by the number of ICO's launched and provides information as to how much was raised through these ICO projects.

claims.claim: Switzerland leads the world in total ICO funds raised, followed by the United States.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: 2017 time period
top 25 ICO countries by funds raised
claims.supporting_quote: Switzerland leads the world in total ICO Funds raised, followed by the United States.

claims.claim: Switzerland ranks only fourth in the number of ICOs launched yet first in total funds raised, so the average Swiss ICO project raises a greater than average amount of funds.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: 2017 data
top 25 ICO countries
claims.supporting_quote: Switzerland is the country with the 4th most ICO's launched but the greatest amount of funds raised in total. Accordingly, the average project in Switzerland is raising a greater than average amount of funds.

claims.claim: Switzerland's disproportionate share of ICO funds raised relative to ICO count is attributable to the fact that many of the world's most successful ICOs are launched there.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
claims.supporting_quote: This can be attributed to the fact that many of the world's most successful ICOs get launched in Switzerland.

claims.claim: Although federal securities law is the main instrument countries use to regulate ICO technology, there is also concern about regulating exchanges, which may fall outside federal securities laws at least in part.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: top 25 ICO countries
claims.supporting_quote: Although (federal) securities law is the main way countries are regulating this technology, there is also concern about the regulation of exchanges within such countries which may fall outside of the federal securities laws, at least in part.

claims.claim: Few governments have prohibited financial investors from investing in ICOs, a greater number have suggested not taking part, and many have issued warnings without any recommendation to citizens either way.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: top 25 ICO countries
claims.supporting_quote: Finally, few governments have prohibited financial investors from investing, but a greater number of governments have suggested not to take part. Many countries have issued warnings, but have not made a suggestion to its citizens as to whether to take part or not.

claims.claim: The comparative summaries of national regulatory responses are necessarily incomplete and require much more analysis before they can be determinative for jurisdictional choice.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: scope of this study
claims.supporting_quote: The summaries provided below on the regulatory responses are naturally incomplete and require much more analysis to be determinative for jurisdictional choices.

claims.claim: The United States was excluded from the comparative jurisdictional analysis because its regulatory setup for cryptocurrencies and DLT business was still too uncertain at the time of publication.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: as of publication in 2018
claims.supporting_quote: The regulatory setup for cryptocurrencies and DLT business was still too uncertain in the United States to be included in the below discussion at the time of publication of this article.

claims.claim: The UK Financial Conduct Authority takes the position that ICOs may be regulated as securities depending on the aspects and rights the coin holder obtains through holding the coin, assessed case by case.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: United Kingdom
claims.supporting_quote: The FCA has taken the position that ICO's may be regulated as securities depending on the different aspects and rights the coin holder obtains through holding the coin.

claims.claim: The FCA has acknowledged that distributed ledger technology has unique aspects capable of working around current regulations.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: United Kingdom
claims.supporting_quote: the FCA has acknowledged that DLT has unique aspects that can work around current regulations.

claims.claim: The Central Bank of Russia has indicated that regulation of ICO and cryptocurrency technology is premature and has therefore declined to issue any regulations controlling ICOs, cryptocurrency, or DLT.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Russian Federation
as of publication
claims.supporting_quote: At the time of publication, the Central Bank of Russia has indicated that the regulation of this technology is premature. For this reason, the Central Bank of Russia has declined to put forth any regulations to control ICO's, cryptocurrency, or DLT.

claims.claim: In Singapore there is no direct regulation of digital tokens under the Securities and Futures Act unless the currency is linked to an ownership or security interest in the issuer's assets or property.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Singapore
claims.supporting_quote: There is no direct regulation under the SFA unless the currency is linked to an ownership or security interest in the issuers assets or property.

claims.claim: If a digital token security falls outside Monetary Authority of Singapore regulation, no duty of fair dealing applies to it.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Singapore
tokens outside MAS regulation
claims.supporting_quote: If the security falls outside the MAS- regulations, there will be no duty of fair dealing.

claims.claim: In Australia, an ICO that falls under the Corporations Act triggers additional disclosure requirements, for example where the ICO constitutes a managed investment scheme.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Australia
claims.supporting_quote: If an ICO/cryptocurrency falls under the Corporations Act, additional disclosures are triggered. For instance, an ICO might trigger a disclosure requirement if the ICO is a managed investment scheme (MIS).

claims.claim: Gibraltar treats DLT regulation as better achieved through the application of principles rather than rigid rules, because the area of law is evolving and innovative.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Gibraltar
claims.supporting_quote: Gibraltar recognizes that this area of the law is evolving and innovative, and as such is better achieved through the "application of principles rather than rigid rules"

claims.claim: Under German law the decisive factor in classifying a token is which rights are associated with it; labels such as participation token, utility token, or payment token give only initial guidance and cannot be relied upon outside a comprehensive and binding regulatory classification.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Germany
BaFin securities supervision
claims.supporting_quote: A prior classification of the token (i.e. as a "participation token", "utility token", or "payment token") can provide initial guidance as to the type of token it is under German law, but is not to be relied upon outside a comprehensive and binding regulatory classification.

claims.claim: The Canadian Securities Administrators apply a four-factor test to determine whether a cryptocurrency must be registered as a security.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Canada
claims.supporting_quote: The CSA applies a four-factor test in determining whether a cryptocurrency have to be registered as securities.

claims.claim: At the time of publication there were no registered marketplaces or alternative trading systems for cryptocurrency in Canada.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Canada
as of publication
claims.supporting_quote: At the time of publication, there were no registered marketplaces or ATS's in Canada.

claims.claim: Israel taxes cryptocurrency as property: profits are subject to capital gains tax at rates between twenty and twenty-five percent, and individuals mining or trading cryptocurrencies in connection with businesses must also pay a seventeen percent value-added tax.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Israel
February 2018 Tax Authority position
claims.supporting_quote: cryptocurrencies will be subject to capital gains tax at rates between twenty percent and twenty-five percent, while individuals mining or trading cryptocurrencies in connection with businesses must pay a seventeen percent value-added tax (VAT) in addition to capital gains tax.

claims.claim: Poland's Ministry of Finance interpretation states that selling or exchanging cryptocurrency for traditional currency, or exchanging one cryptocurrency for another, could create a VAT tax obligation.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Poland
April 2018 tax interpretation
claims.supporting_quote: the sale and exchange of cryptocurrencies into traditional currency and vice versa, as well as the exchange of one cryptocurrency for another, could create a VAT tax obligation.

claims.claim: The People's Republic of China has banned ICOs entirely, including the offering of coins and the exchanges used to trade them, on the view that ICOs hurt the market through potential deception and fraud.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: China
claims.supporting_quote: The People Republic of China have taken a firm stance against ICO's, banning them entirely.

claims.claim: Because cryptocurrencies are not issued by foreign central banks, Costa Rica does not consider them foreign currency and they cannot fall under the regulations of the exchange regime.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Costa Rica
claims.supporting_quote: As cryptocurrencies are also not issued by foreign central banks, they cannot be considered foreign currency and so cannot fall under the regulations of the exchange regime.

claims.claim: The National Bank of Slovakia takes the view that cryptocurrencies are not money because countries enjoy monetary sovereignty.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Slovakia
claims.supporting_quote: The national bank takes the view that cryptocurrencies are not considered money because countries enjoy monetary sovereignty.

claims.claim: The National Bank of Serbia holds that financial institutions may not participate in ICOs or other cryptocurrency investments because cryptocurrencies are not legal tender.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Serbia
claims.supporting_quote: Serbia has taken the position that financial institutional are not allowed to participate in ICO's or other cryptocurrency investments because they are not legal tender.

claims.claim: Sweden's Finansinspektionen treats ICOs as investment products that may be traded, and although there is no explicit ban on financial companies raising money through ICOs, no Swedish company had attempted to do so.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: Sweden
as of publication
claims.supporting_quote: Although there is no explicit ban on financial companies raising money through ICO's, no Swedish company has attempted to do so yet.

claims.claim: Across the top 25 ICO jurisdictions the majority permit ICOs and cryptocurrencies or do not explicitly prohibit them, and only a very small minority has banned them outright.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: top 25 ICO jurisdictions
claims.supporting_quote: The majority of the countries examined in this study permit ICO's and cryptocurrencies or do not explicitly prohibit them.

claims.claim: World governments largely either apply existing laws to cryptocurrencies or wait to see how other countries react to the crypto evolution.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: top 25 ICO jurisdictions
claims.supporting_quote: For the most part, the general view of the world governments appears to be that they are using existing laws to regulate cryptocurrencies or wait to see how other countries react to the crypto evolution.

claims.claim: Regulatory efforts toward ICOs take several forms or permutations of them, including regulating ICOs, cryptocurrencies, and DLT, mandating compliance programs, and regulating exchanges.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
scope_conditions: top 25 ICO jurisdictions
claims.supporting_quote: Regulatory efforts can take several forms but appear to involve some of the following approaches or permutations thereof: regulating ICOs, regulating cryptocurrencies, regulating DLT, mandating compliance programs, regulating exchanges,

claims.claim: The deep architecture of a digital world regulates behavior in many ways, and those regulatory effects cannot be seen or understood unless one examines the nature of the underlying code and how it operates.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: a world of ubiquitous computing where code structures everyday experience
claims.supporting_quote: The deep architecture of a digital world can regulate in a host of ways, ways that one cannot begin to see (or understand) unless you consider the nature of such code and how it operates.

claims.claim: Lawyers have historically been most effective and most socially useful when acting as transaction engineers who facilitate new business and social relationships, and the engineering of the near future will largely be code based.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: periods of fast paced technological change
claims.supporting_quote: Historically, lawyers have been at their most effective – and socially useful - when they operate as "transaction engineers," i.e., facilitating new forms of business and other social relationships.6 It seems obvious that the "engineering" of the near-future will, to a large extent, be code-based.

claims.claim: The ability to understand and communicate with coders, as distinct from professional coding competence, is a necessary skill for the lawyer of the future, so law students benefit from grasping the basic concepts and power of coding.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: legal practice in a code based economy
claims.supporting_quote: However, we do believe that the ability to understand and communicate with coders is a necessary skill for the lawyer of the future. As such, we think that law students will benefit from understanding the basic concepts and power of coding.

claims.claim: The traditional knowledge transmission model of education is ill suited to a world of fast paced change and easy access to information, because prior experience may not be relevant to a fast changing reality and information is always one search away.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: fast paced technological change
low cost universal access to information
claims.supporting_quote: But, this model seems ill-suited to a world of fast-paced change and easy access to information. Prior experience may not be relevant to a fast-changing reality and information is only ever one Google search away.

claims.claim: That the technologies driving social change remain a mystery to most people is itself a problem, so practical technical knowledge must be integrated into many fields of education, with coding and data analysis as the starting point.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: education across many fields, not only law
claims.supporting_quote: For many of us, the underlying technologies that are driving social change remain a mystery, and that is a problem. Practical technical knowledge needs to be integrated into many fields of education. Coding and data analysis seem a good starting point.

claims.claim: In early Silicon Valley the contractual mechanisms lawyers designed, together with the lawyer dominated market for reputation, reduced information asymmetries between entrepreneurs and investors and were necessary to bring the demand and supply sides of venture capital together effectively.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: venture capital markets with young and inexperienced entrepreneurs
Silicon Valley from the early 1970s
claims.supporting_quote: Finally, the contractual mechanisms and the lawyer-dominated market for reputation reduced the information asymmetries between the entrepreneurs and investors and, as such, were necessary to bring the demand-side and supply-side of "venture capital" together effectively.

claims.claim: A transaction engineer is a crucial intermediary who brings together, in a safe environment, parties holding different but mutually compatible interests and expertise.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
claims.supporting_quote: In this sense, we can see how lawyers functioned as "transaction engineers," i.e., crucial intermediaries that brought together in a "safe" environment various parties with different but mutually compatible interests and expertise.

claims.claim: Lawyers have often failed to perform the function of active transaction engineer and have instead become a hindrance or obstacle to transactions.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
claims.supporting_quote: The problem, however, is that lawyers have often failed to perform this function of being active transaction engineers and have become a hindrance or obstacle to transactions.

claims.claim: The major cause of lawyers obstructing transactions is the tendency to standardize or proceduralize legal solutions and to use standard form templates, because fixed standardized solutions imposed on complex, dynamic transactions produce frustration and difficulties.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: complex, dynamic transactions
claims.supporting_quote: This can happen for many reasons but the tendency to standardize – or "proceduralize" - legal solutions and to employ standard form "templates" is one major factor. Fixed and standardized solutions are imposed on complex, dynamic transactions resulting in frustration and difficulties.

claims.claim: The result of this pattern is reputational: lawyers have developed a reputation as the least trusted of professions.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
claims.supporting_quote: As a result, lawyers have developed a reputation as the least trusted of professions.

claims.claim: Legal tech will profoundly disrupt the legal profession, and because these technologies are code based, lawyers must be able to understand and talk about code in order to participate in designing them.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: legal technologies built on software code
claims.supporting_quote: "Legal tech" will profoundly disrupt the legal profession18 and since these technologies are code-based lawyers need to be able to understand and talk about code to participate in the design of such legal technologies

claims.claim: Since companies are increasingly managed by and run on software code, facilitating transactions, that is, acting as an active transaction engineer, now involves coding.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: businesses built around code based products or services
claims.supporting_quote: Since all companies are now increasingly managed by and run on software code, facilitating transactions – i.e., being an active transaction engineer - involves coding.

claims.claim: Junior legal professionals and legal support staff are the first casualties of the Legal Tech evolution, because applications will soon perform most junior lawyer work without the human elements that create imprecision, flaws, inaccuracies, possible lawsuits and delay.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: continued decentralization of legal services by startups
claims.supporting_quote: Junior legal professionals and legal support staff are likely the first victims of the Legal Tech evolution.32 Legal Tech applications will be able to perform most of the junior lawyers' work soon without the human elements that create imprecision, flaws, inaccuracies, possible lawsuits, and delay.

claims.claim: The most important consequence of legal startups is that the legal profession will be forced to innovate in perpetuity, a task that overextended and cumbersome legal organizations which have lost the capacity for rapid re-invention cannot easily accomplish.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: incumbent law firms and legal departments facing startup competition
claims.supporting_quote: Second, and most importantly, the legal profession will be forced by such startup companies to innovate in perpetuity, a task that is not easily accomplished by overextended and – often – cumbersome legal organizations that have lost the capacity for rapid re-invention.

claims.claim: Contrary to commentators who predict the end of lawyers, the authors reject that claim but hold that lawyers of the future can only function as effective transaction engineers if they understand the power of code.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: lawyers seeking to function as transaction engineers in a digital economy
claims.supporting_quote: We certainly don't make this claim, but we do think that if the lawyers of the future are to function as effective transaction engineers, they are going to need to understand the power of code.

claims.claim: Lawyers of the future will need to act as project managers or at least as active participants in the multi-disciplinary teams that design the solutions and transactions of the future.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: design of code dependent solutions and transactions
claims.supporting_quote: Firstly, lawyers of the future will need to be able to assume the role of project managers or, at least, active participants in the new multi- disciplinary teams that are going to design the solutions/transactions of the future.

claims.claim: Many new innovation driven firms that replaced hierarchy with a best-idea-wins culture have struggled to maintain that governance model and to fulfill their initial promise.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: fast growth technology companies with few assets and employees
claims.supporting_quote: Significantly, however, many such "new" firms have often struggled to maintain this new governance model and fulfill their initial promise.

claims.claim: Because blockchain network nodes verify, validate and audit transactions both before and after execution, the model is safer than a traditional one in which transactions can only be accomplished through third party intermediaries such as a bank, judiciary or notary.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: peer to peer networks using a distributed consensus model
claims.supporting_quote: verify, validate and audit transactions before and after they are executed. 49 This is safer than a traditional model in which transactions can only be accomplished through third-party intermediaries, such as a bank, judiciary or notary.

claims.claim: Cryptographic hashing makes tampering with blockchain records extremely difficult because even a minuscule change produces a different hash value, rendering manipulation instantly and readily detectable.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: records secured by cryptographic hash functions
claims.supporting_quote: The use of cryptographic hashes makes tampering with blockchain records even more difficult, if not impossible. 52 Cryptographic hashes comprise complex algorithms. Even a minuscule change to the blockchain will result in a different hash value, making manipulation instantly and readily detectable.

claims.claim: Blockchain replaces intermediaries, bureaucracy and old fashioned procedures with the four Cs of code, connectivity, crowd and collaboration, which increases openness and speed while significantly reducing costs.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
claims.supporting_quote: Intermediaries, bureaucracy and old-fashioned procedures are replaced by the 4 Cs: code, connectivity, crowd, and collaboration. 55 The technology increases openness and speed, while at the same time significantly reducing costs.

claims.claim: A smart contract is computer program code that enables the verification, execution and enforcement of specific terms and conditions of a contractual arrangement.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
claims.supporting_quote: A smart contract is a computer program code that enables the verification, execution, and enforcement of specific terms and conditions of a contractual arrangement.

claims.claim: Smart contract use scales with device connectivity: the more devices are connected to each other, the more smart contracts will be used to execute and enforce legal transactions, and they are already disrupting traditional legal assumptions, doctrines and concepts.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: growth of the Internet of Things
claims.supporting_quote: The more devices are connected to each other, the more "smart contracts" will be used to execute and enforce "legal transactions." There is no doubt that smart contracts are already disrupting traditional legal assumptions, doctrines, and concepts.

claims.claim: A decentralized autonomous organization is merely computer code with no directors, managers or employees, its governance structure built with software, code and smart contracts running on a public decentralized blockchain platform.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: DAOs built on public platforms, in most cases Ethereum
claims.supporting_quote: DAOs are "merely" computer code. They don't have any directors, managers or employees. The governance structure is built with and on software, code and smart contracts that ran on a public decentralized blockchain platform (in most cases Ethereum).

claims.claim: As software code automates procedures and tasks, the focus of knowledge work shifts from the routine application of procedures to designing the systems and standardized functions that machines then perform.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: a flatter, decentralized and automated economy
claims.supporting_quote: DOAs fit in the flatter, decentralized and automated world. With software code automating procedures and tasks, the focus of "knowledge work" is shifting from the routine "application of procedures" to designing the systems and standardized functions that are then performed by machines.

claims.claim: Law programs have been slow to adapt to these technological developments and most students are still being prepared for a hierarchical, centralized and proceduralized world.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: law school curricula as of 2018
claims.supporting_quote: Unfortunately, law programs have been slow to adapt to these technological developments. Most students are still being prepared for a hierarchical, centralized and "proceduralized" world.

claims.claim: Because the new solutions rewarded by the future labor market will be code based, an understanding of code and coding will be essential to participate effectively in the digital world.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: a labor market that rewards designing rather than following procedures
claims.supporting_quote: And since these new solutions will be code-based, an understanding of code and coding will be essential to participate effectively in our digital world.

claims.claim: In a digital world trust can be embedded directly in software code, and recent interest in smart contracts suggests this will be a significant growth area in the near future.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: digital transactions where code can carry contractual terms
claims.supporting_quote: In a digital world, trust can be embedded in software code. Recent interest in smart contracts suggests that this is going to be a significant growth area in the near-future.

claims.claim: As machine to machine interaction becomes normal in an Internet of Things environment, trust ceases to be primarily a legal question and becomes a technical and design problem.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: machine to machine transactions in an Internet of Things environment
claims.supporting_quote: code is also crucial in machine-to-machine (M2M) based transactions. As M2M interaction becomes normal in an Internet of Things environment, the issue of trust becomes a technical and design problem.

claims.claim: Cybersecurity should not be addressed by introducing more law in books; law students should instead look for technology based solutions and at minimum acquire the knowledge needed to evaluate such solutions against the alternatives.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: cloud delivered software and Internet of Things environments
claims.supporting_quote: But instead of combatting "cybersecurity" with the introduction of "more law in books," law students should look for technology-based solutions. At the very least, they need to have the necessary knowledge to evaluate technology-based solutions and compare them with the alternatives.

claims.claim: Building lawyers' capacity to think about the social and ethical implications of code is both essential and inevitable, but saying anything sensible about the ethics of technology first requires understanding coding and coders.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: ethical questions raised by automation, artificial intelligence and driverless vehicles
claims.supporting_quote: Building the capacity of the lawyers of the future to think about the social and ethical implications of code is both essential and inevitable. But, to say something sensible about the ethical aspects of technology, it is necessary to understand both more about coding and coders.

claims.claim: DAOs will eventually overtake any organization that lacks their incentives and efficiencies, and because DAOs are cheap and straightforward to clone this will potentially lead to more competition.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: comparison with organizations lacking DAO incentives and efficiencies
claims.supporting_quote: we also concluded (as we did in class) that DAOs will eventually overtake any organization which lacks these incentives and efficiencies. Moreover, DAOs are cheap and straightforward to "clone," which will potentially lead to more competition.

claims.claim: Existing blockchains and DAOs still lack genuine decentralization, and there are currently no true DAOs: Bitcoin's proof of work protocol has produced mining pools because of economies of scale and unbalanced reward structures.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: proof of work blockchains as of 2018
claims.supporting_quote: In our discussion, the following weaknesses were highlighted. There is still a lack of decentralization (there are currently no "true" DAOs). For instance, Bitcoin's proof of work protocol has led to "mining pools" because of economies of scale and unbalanced reward structures.

claims.claim: Anonymity in blockchain organizations makes them prone to Sybil attacks and 51 percent attacks, and anonymity combined with autonomy has led to many hacks.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: anonymous and autonomous blockchain organizations
claims.supporting_quote: Also, the anonymity in blockchain organizations means that they are prone to "Sybil attacks" and "51% attacks." We also discussed the many examples in which the anonymity (and autonomy) have led to hacks.

claims.claim: In a truly decentralized system any mistake, such as a stolen or lost password or a programming bug, is permanent and irrevocable.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: truly decentralized systems with no reversal authority
claims.supporting_quote: Remember that in a truly decentralized system, any mistakes (stolen/lost passwords, programming bugs, etc.) are permanent and irrevocable.

claims.claim: A reputation verification platform matters because trust created through an eternal reputational record would be open to review and driven by proper incentives.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: blockchain based reputation systems that reward trustful parties and punish bad actors
claims.supporting_quote: This was considered to be important because if the trust were to be created through an eternal reputational record, it would be open to review and driven by proper incentives.

claims.claim: The real design challenge for consensus protocols is to find a proof of stake protocol that offers both trust and security without unintentionally creating just another centralized validation system.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: blockchain consensus protocol design
claims.supporting_quote: The students understood that the real challenge is to find a "proof of stake" protocol that offers both trust and security (without unintentionally creating just another centralized validation system).

claims.claim: The Coding for Lawyers course is not about teaching students how to code but about making them realize how important it is to think about their relationship with new technology and with technology experts.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: the course as taught in Europe and the United States
claims.supporting_quote: It is not about teaching students "how to code," but about making them realize how important it is to think about our relationship with new technology and technology experts.

claims.claim: Coders and developers do not always understand the industry or business environment they target with their software solutions, nor do they always consider the trust or ethical issues raised by the technology based business solutions they implement.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: technology based business solutions built by developers
claims.supporting_quote: Coders, programmers, and other developers do not always understand the industry or business environment they target with their software solutions. Nor do they always consider the trust or ethical issues when implementing technology-based business solutions.

claims.claim: Developers are not trained to consider business context or ethics because most tech education focuses almost exclusively on technical training and skills, so a parallel reconfiguration of technical education is required alongside the reform of legal education.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: current technical education curricula
claims.supporting_quote: They are not trained to think in this way. Most tech- education is almost exclusively focused on technical training and skills. A parallel reconfiguration in our technical education is also required.

claims.claim: Co-creation partnerships between developers and non-developers will be crucial to building a better digital future, and understanding coding is what enables lawyers to engage constructively with coders, programmers and other software developers.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: multi-disciplinary software development projects
claims.supporting_quote: "Co-creation" involving partnerships between developers and non- developers will be crucial to building a "better" digital future. And understanding coding enables lawyers to constructively engage with coders, programmers, and other software developers.

claims.claim: If standardized legal work and legal research can be performed by algorithms, the result is an opportunity rather than a threat, because it frees lawyer time for assisting clients with the new and very specific challenges of the digital world.
claims.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967
scope_conditions: successful algorithmic automation of standardized legal work
claims.supporting_quote: If the "standardized work" and legal research activities can be performed by algorithms, there is more time for assisting the client with the new and very specific challenges of the digital world.

claims.claim: Internet based platform businesses and distributed ledger technology businesses have not reached their full potential, and the core factor holding them back is worldwide decreasing trust in the internet together with under developed trust in decentralized technology solutions.
claims.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Gopinath Sivalingam, Reputation Protocol for the Internet of Trust - Conceptual Whitepaper (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3266953
scope_conditions: internet based platform businesses
distributed ledger technology businesses
claims.supporting_quote: Multiple studies, data, and anecdotal evidence suggest that one core factor that undermines their evolution is the worldwide decreasing trust in the internet and under-developed trust in decentralized technology solutions.

claims.claim: Adding more regulations, processes and procedures cannot restore confidence in institutions, because the traditional trust and cohesion mechanisms have already reached their limits.
claims.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Gopinath Sivalingam, Reputation Protocol for the Internet of Trust - Conceptual Whitepaper (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3266953
scope_conditions: attempts to restore institutionalized trust
claims.supporting_quote: To restore confidence in the "old world", efforts have tended to focus on introducing and implementing more regulations, processes, and procedures. Yet, the traditional trust and cohesion mechanisms have reached their limits.

claims.claim: Digitized and automated trust is not a stable substitute for institutional trust, because it is experiencing crises of its own that undermine the proliferation of value enhancing internet based platform businesses and distributed ledger technology businesses.
claims.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Gopinath Sivalingam, Reputation Protocol for the Internet of Trust - Conceptual Whitepaper (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3266953
scope_conditions: trust migrated from organizations to machines and algorithms
claims.supporting_quote: Yet, this digitized trust is experiencing its own crises which undermines the proliferation of value-enhancing internet-based platform businesses and DLT businesses.

claims.claim: The trust humans place in machines on the internet has never been verified, because neither centralized nor decentralized authentication engines have typically confirmed that trust or otherwise enabled a trusting environment for internet based transactions.
claims.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Gopinath Sivalingam, Reputation Protocol for the Internet of Trust - Conceptual Whitepaper (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3266953
scope_conditions: human to machine interaction on the internet
claims.supporting_quote: Yet no centralized or decentralized authentication engine has typically verified the trust humans place in machines or otherwise enabled a trusting environment for internet-based transactions.

claims.claim: Today's internet is designed for hierarchical societal structures on an underlying authoritative trust model, and that traditional hierarchical trust model carries many inefficiencies including serious cyber security vulnerabilities.
claims.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Gopinath Sivalingam, Reputation Protocol for the Internet of Trust - Conceptual Whitepaper (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3266953
claims.supporting_quote: Worse yet, today's internet is designed for hierarchical societal structures and with an underlying authoritative trust model. Many inefficiencies are associated with the traditional hierarchical trust model including serious cyber security vulnerabilities.

claims.claim: The centralized version of the internet cannot scale to the thirty to fifty billion connected devices that experts expect by 2020, which is why decentralized authentication solutions for internet of things devices are needed.
claims.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Gopinath Sivalingam, Reputation Protocol for the Internet of Trust - Conceptual Whitepaper (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3266953
scope_conditions: projected device counts by the year 2020
claims.supporting_quote: By the year 2020 the majority of experts estimates that a total of 30 to 50 billion devices will connect to the internet.8 The prevailing opinion of these researchers suggests that the centralized version of the internet cannot scale to that level.

claims.claim: Displayed net feedback scores are a poor reputation instrument because they encourage Pollyanna assessments of reputation and are far from the best predictor of performance available in the data.
claims.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Gopinath Sivalingam, Reputation Protocol for the Internet of Trust - Conceptual Whitepaper (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3266953
scope_conditions: eBay feedback data from 1999
claims.supporting_quote: However, the net feedback scores that eBay displays encourages Pollyanna assessments of reputations, and is far from the best predictor available.
