claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: At their worst, DAOs result in ponzi schemes and rug pulls that undermine the future of web3 and associated upgrades for humanity.

claims.claim: Poorly executed DAOs exhibit a recognizable cluster of pathologies, including siphoned coins, distracted and robo voters, centralization, DAO washing by founders, and absent decentralized governance, and these pathologies drive mid-term and long-term DAO failure.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: Several of the identifiable downsides include: siphoned coins, distracted and robo voters, centralization, DAO washing by founders, lack of decentralized governance, and other pitfalls that could end up in mid-term and long-term DAO failure.

claims.claim: Rug pulls grew sharply as a share of crypto crime: of the $7.7 billion in total illicit crypto revenue in 2021, 37 percent came from rug pulls, up from 1 percent of illicit revenue in 2020.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: 2021 data
measured as a share of total illicit crypto revenue
claims.supporting_quote: In 2021 alone, the total illicit revenue from crypto scams was $7.7 billion; 37% of that total resulted from "rug pulls," an increase from the 1% of total illicit revenue in 2020.

claims.claim: Fundraiser DAOs are structurally fragile because they typically lack incentives for meaningful community engagement, so they dissipate once the hype that created them fades.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: DAOs formed primarily to raise funds
claims.supporting_quote: Fundraiser DAOs are vulnerable in multiple ways. They often lack incentives for meaningful community engagement and tend to dissipate with the hype.

claims.claim: Governance by fungible tokens lets whales control a fundraiser DAO, which is antithetical to decentralized governance, and selling purchasable voting power via fungible tokens creates the risk of hostile takeover or looting.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: governance rights attached to fungible, purchasable tokens
claims.supporting_quote: Governance through fungible tokens in fundraiser DAOs allows whales to control the DAO, which is antithetical to the idea of DAOs overall and decentralized governance of DAOs specifically. More specifically, selling purchasable voting power via fungible tokens risks hostile takeovers or looting.

claims.claim: The author contests the myth that DAOs are generally run by scammers: many DAOs and users have indeed fallen victim to rug pulls, but most of those rug pulls trace to the absence of decentralized governance in fundraiser DAOs rather than to DAOs as such.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: applies to fundraiser DAOs lacking decentralized governance
claims.supporting_quote: While it is true that many DAOs and DAO users have fallen victim to the infamous rug-pulls, most of these rug pulls are associated with the lack of decentralized governance in fundraiser DAOs.

claims.claim: DAO projects accounted for a material share of the largest crypto frauds of the year: two of the top six crypto rug pulls in 2021 were DAO projects.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: top six crypto rug pulls by size
claims.supporting_quote: Of the top six crypto rug pulls in 2021, two were DAO projects.

claims.claim: A DAO token sale can be drained at the moment of closing: in the Anubis DAO sale 13597 ETH was removed from the token sale pool and sent to another address as the sale was about to close, and because the launch platform had not been compromised the loss was attributed to an inside rug pull.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: Anubis DAO token sale on the Copper platform, October 2021
claims.supporting_quote: As the sale was about to close, 13597 ETH was removed from the token sale pool and sent to another address. Allegations of a rug pull ensued because the launch platform Copper had not been compromised.

claims.claim: Most DAOs that suffer unethical behavior and rug pulls are abused by insiders, and this is possible because insiders are not properly governed and hold too much control over the DAO; true decentralized community governance removes insider and council control over keys and code.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: DAOs where councils or privileged insiders retain key and code control
claims.supporting_quote: Most DAOs that fall victim to unethical behavior and rug pulls are subject to abuses from insiders. Typically these insider abuses are possible because the insiders are not governed properly and have too much control over the DAO.

claims.claim: Insider knowledge of contract internals is itself an attack surface: at Snowdog DAO an insider who knew a challenge key embedded in the DAO contract backran the anticipated buyback and sold tokens ahead of it.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: Snowdog DAO on the Avalanche protocol
insider holding a contract challenge key
claims.supporting_quote: For example, Snowdog DAO suffered an alleged rug-pull when an insider who knew a "challenge key" (a part of the DAOs contract), backran the anticipated buyback and began selling tokens.

claims.claim: Insider rug pulls are not the only exploit path: a DAO can also be attacked from the outside whenever its governance grants voting power through fungible tokens.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: governance voting power is denominated in fungible tokens
claims.supporting_quote: But these inside rug pulls are not the only exploitative mechanism within DAOs. DAOs can also be exploited from the outside if the DAO's governance allows fungible voting power.

claims.claim: The absence of proper decentralized governance built on non-fungible tokens is a key common denominator across DAO failures and rug pulls.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: The lack of proper decentralized governance with non-fungible tokens is a key common denominator among DAO failures and rug pulls.

claims.claim: Dispersed, passive token holders cannot defend a DAO: because power in Build Finance DAO was not decentralized, the silent majority of token holders lacked the voting power to block the takeover, after which the attacker minted and sold tokens by draining liquidity pools.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: low participation among dispersed token holders
claims.supporting_quote: Because of the lack of decentralized power in the Build Finance DAO, the silent majority of token holders did not have enough voting power to prevent the takeover. As a result, the attacker minted and sold various tokens by draining liquidity pools.

claims.claim: Defending a DAO against attackers and looters, and punishing self-dealing, requires sustainable decentralized governance built on non-fungible tokens rather than tradable voting power.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: The takeover of the Build Finance DAO highlights the need for sustainable decentralized governance solutions with non-fungible tokens to defend the DAO from attackers/looters and punish self- dealing.

claims.claim: Governance in most DAOs is severely underdeveloped, which leaves a minority of stakeholders defining governance, and that minority control in turn produces mediocre and poorly developed proposals.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: DAOs still in early governance experimentation
claims.supporting_quote: Governance is severely underdeveloped in most DAOs which results typically in a minority of stakeholders that define governance. This, in turn, often result in mediocre and poorly-developed proposals.

claims.claim: The author rejects the claim that DAOs are ungovernable: the shortcomings are real, but ongoing experimentation with DAO governance designs is gradually identifying workable decentralized governance solutions.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: While these shortcomings in the DAO ecosystem are real, the experimentation with DAO governance designs is gradually identifying workable decentralized governance solutions for the DAO ecosystem.

claims.claim: Workable DAO governance should account for reputation with non-fungible tokens or weighted keys rather than fungible tokens, so that voting weight tracks reputation instead of purchasing power.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: 1. Non-fungible Tokens or weighted keys, among other electronic accounting methods as accounting for reputation score NOT fungible tokens

claims.claim: DAO governance should use a two vote model that distinguishes a loosely coupled vote, where no reputation is at stake, from a tightly coupled vote, where the voter's reputation is at stake.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: 2. Two vote model a) loosely coupled vote (no reputation at stake), b) tightly coupled vote (reputation at stake)

claims.claim: Reputation in a DAO should be generated only for long term valuable work and for the policing of work, and never for business development work.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: 3. Reputation generated ONLY for long term valuable work and policing of work NOT for business development work

claims.claim: Smart contracts that govern fungible currency exchanges are engineered for irreversible, unreviewable, programmed self execution, and that design makes the business structure of web3 more rigid.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: smart contracts involving fungible currency exchange
claims.supporting_quote: Yet, smart contracts involving fungible currency exchanges are designed to guarantee irreversible, unreviewable, programmed self execution. As such, they create a more rigid structure for business in web3.

claims.claim: Code is law fails as a complete business ordering because business ventures very rarely proceed exactly as written in smart contract code: real business relationships are far messier and more multivalent than a series of smart contracts can predict.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: In reality, very rarely does any business venture proceed exactly as planned in smart contract code because the reality of business relationships is far more messy and multivalent than can be predicted by a series of smart contracts.

claims.claim: Effective business dealing requires that counterparties have confidence a fair resolution will occur when transactions do not develop as planned, which purely self executing code cannot supply.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: To do business effectively, counterparties need confidence that a fair resolution will occur when transactions do not develop as planned.

claims.claim: Effective human-centric DAO governance is the remedy for rigid smart contract rules that undermine business activities requiring more flexibility in web3 and the metaverse.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: business activities that require flexibility in web3 and the metaverse
claims.supporting_quote: Effective human-centric DAO governance solves the issue of rid smart contract rules that undermine business activities that require more flexibility in web3 and the metaverse.

claims.claim: Anonymous decentralized networks can encourage troll behavior because participants feel safe attacking others without retribution, and in a DAO that trolling destabilizes the organization and creates friction between members and the DAO.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: anonymous participation without reputational stake
claims.supporting_quote: In the DAO context, trolling behavior destabilizes the organization and causes friction between members and the DAO.

claims.claim: The friction generated by anonymous trolling can be mitigated through incentivized reputational architecture governed by protocols the community itself decides on, so anonymity does not have to corrupt DAO governance.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: reputational architecture is implemented correctly and community governed
claims.supporting_quote: By contrast, if implemented correctly, anonymity significantly upgrades DAO governance. The friction that arises from anonymous trolling can be mitigated through the implementation of incentivized reputational architecture governed by protocols decided upon by the community.

claims.claim: Properly implemented anonymity strengthens decentralized governance because it lets individuals relate without the inherited biases of predecessor generations and a lifetime inside centralized power structures.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: anonymity is properly implemented
claims.supporting_quote: If properly implemented, anonymity strengthens decentralized governance by taking out parts of the human nature that hold business and society back. First and foremost, anonymity allows individuals to relate to each other without the inherited biases of generations of predecessors

claims.claim: Anonymity lets information flow from the edges of the system, from individuals who would have no agency in centralized structures, and such inputs are much less likely to materialize if DAO participants know each other.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: anonymity is preserved among DAO participants
claims.supporting_quote: allows information to flow from the edges of the system with individuals who would have no agency in centralized structures but can add invaluable input into the system. Such inputs will not materialize, or are much less likely to materialize, if DAO participants know each other.

claims.claim: True anonymity remains eternally difficult to attain with existing web3 technology, yet anonymity in DAO governance is the holy grail of decentralized web3 business and society.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: given existing web3 technology
claims.supporting_quote: while it is eternally difficult with existing technology to attain true anonymity in web3 systems, anonymity in DAO governance is the wholly grail of decentralized web3 business and society.

claims.claim: A meaningful reputation governance and accounting mechanism for motivating business and governance participation is what encourages mutually beneficial contributions to a DAO community.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: a meaningful reputation governance and accounting mechanism is in place
claims.supporting_quote: A meaningful reputation governance and accounting mechanism for motivating business and governance participation encourages mutually beneficial contributions to the community.

claims.claim: Traditional work in centralized structures is prone to extrinsically motivated engagement, which intensifies principal agent problems and produces suboptimal outcomes because a principal dictates where, what, and when workers perform.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: centralized employment structures with a directing principal
claims.supporting_quote: The traditional work environment in centralized structures is prone to extrinsically motivated work engagement which intensifies principal agent problems.

claims.claim: In a DAO, a member's influence and outcomes are determined by the value that member's contributions add to the shared work product, rather than by position in a hierarchy.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: contribution value is measurable and governs influence
claims.supporting_quote: DAOs allow influence and outcomes of DAO members to be determined by the value a DAO member's contributions to the shared work product.

claims.claim: High value contribution is self-amplifying in a DAO: when a member adds substantial value, other token holders want to add their skills to the same work product through a policing engagement, which focuses all members' joint efforts on the highest possible value proposition.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: members can observe and join high value work products
claims.supporting_quote: Moreover, if a DAO member adds substantial value to the DAO, other DAO token holders will want to add their skills to the same work product via a policing engagement which focuses all DAO members' joint efforts on the highest possible value proposition.

claims.claim: Braintrust demonstrates that innovation in work structure does not cure governance design: despite redefining work outcomes, it uses a suboptimal one token, one vote model that grants proportional control over network governance.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: governance by one token, one vote
claims.supporting_quote: Despite its advances in innovation for redefining work outcomes, Braintrust uses a suboptimal governance model with a one token, one vote system for proportional control over how the network is governed.

claims.claim: Work-to-earn DAOs must leave it entirely to each member how much time they contribute; DAOs that impose quotas and participation requirements may not be sustainable long-term in a value-to-efforts workflow environment.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: work-to-earn DAOs seeking to attract long-term talent
claims.supporting_quote: In order to attract long-term talent, it needs to be always up to each individual DAO member how much time they put in. DAOs that create quota and participation requirements may not be sustainable long-term in a work-to-earn value-to-efforts workflow environment.

claims.claim: Proof of personhood projects such as Proof of Humanity and UBI DAO fail because they rest on web-of-trust theory, which has been proven not to work long-term given the sockpuppet attacks that are inevitable in that design.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: identity systems built on web-of-trust vouching
claims.supporting_quote: Of course, these attempts are all falling victim to web-of-trust theory that has been proven to not work long-term because the sockpuppet attacks that are inevitable in this design.

claims.claim: Microdemocracy combined with proper incentive design can reverse the decreasing voter participation that undermines representative democracies.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
scope_conditions: decentralized voting infrastructure is in place
claims.supporting_quote: Microdemocracy and proper incentive design can reverse decreasing voter participation that undermines representative democracies.

claims.claim: Centralization and monopolies are a threat to market liquidity because they can carry too much mass or too much velocity, and an imbalance in either direction, too much mass and too little velocity or too little mass, damages the market.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: When there is too much mass and not enough velocity, it can gunk up the engine - when there is too little mass in the market, it can be cleared too quickly. Centralization and monopolies are a threat to market liquidity as they can have too much mass or too much velocity.

claims.claim: Decentralized structures outperform centralized ones on liquidity because in them market mass and velocity are uncorrelated, which yields more stable and predictable liquidity.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: Decentralized structures are better because mass and velocity are uncorrelated

claims.claim: Diversity of viewpoints is severely diminished when power is centralized, whereas information technology allows a global network open to members of diverse values and backgrounds to form.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: Diversity of viewpoints is severely diminished when power is centralized. Information technology allows a global network of people to form, open to members of diverse values and backgrounds.

claims.claim: Flatter markets with more diverse interests and talents are more effective and efficient at truth discovery, including price discovery and the identification of ideal solutions to new problems, and decentralization promotes that diversity by improving member autonomy and freedom.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783
claims.supporting_quote: Flatter markets with more diverse interests and talents are more effective and efficient at achieving truth discovery, like price discovery and the identification of ideal solutions to arbitrary new problems that arise.

claims.claim: Valuation metrics developed for legacy assets apply only in a limited way to digital assets, so importing them wholesale produces unreliable digital asset valuations.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: digital assets as of 2022
claims.supporting_quote: Existing valuation metrics for legacy assets only limitedly apply in the context of digital assets.

claims.claim: Digital asset valuation uncertainty is produced by the combination of an immature digital asset market and a valuation infrastructure, legal, accounting, finance, technology, and back office, that was not built for these assets.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: current state of the digital asset market
claims.supporting_quote: The valuation infrastructure in the current legal, accounting, finance, technology, and back-office framework in combination with the immaturity of the digital asset market create an environment where digital asset valuation continues to be a mystery.

claims.claim: Although many traditional assets also resist full assessment, the absence of established pricing standards for digital assets makes the loss of valuation accuracy for financial reporting worse than in traditional markets.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: financial reporting context
claims.supporting_quote: While many traditional assets also cannot be fully assessed, the lack of valuation accuracy for financial reporting is exacerbated by the lack of established pricing standards for digital assets.

claims.claim: The accounting definition of fair value may not apply to digital assets, with the consequence that correct valuation of digital assets for financial reporting purposes may be impossible.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: under existing accounting terminology such as FASB 157 and IFRS 13
claims.supporting_quote: The definition of fair value under existing accounting terminology may not apply to digital assets.2 As a result, the correct valuation of digital assets may not be possible for financial reporting issues.

claims.claim: Dual listing narrows bid ask spreads in traditional markets by injecting liquidity, but crypto markets behave differently: price differences between two exchanges can reach upwards of five percent during peak trading times.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: peak trading times
assets listed on multiple crypto exchanges
claims.supporting_quote: For traditional markets, when a security is dual- listed, we see the bid-ask spread decrease because additional liquidity is being injected into the market. This differs from the crypto market where the difference between the two exchanges can reach upwards of 5% during peak trading times.5

claims.claim: Digital asset exchanges have no closing prices, so digital asset managers cannot rely on the closing price convention that underpins traditional valuation practice.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: digital asset exchanges
claims.supporting_quote: Because digital asset exchanges do not have closing prices, digital asset managers cannot simply use the closing price for given asset.

claims.claim: Because digital asset valuation methodologies vary significantly, the tradeoffs among them leave digital asset managers with meaningful valuation discretion.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: absence of uniform valuation standards
claims.supporting_quote: Digital asset valuation methodologies vary significantly. Tradeoffs between such methodologies allow for some valuation discretion between digital asset managers.

claims.claim: Even for the most liquid level one digital assets, managers may choose between the price on a favored exchange and an aggregate across exchanges, so the same asset can be reported at different values by different managers.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: quoting level 1 digital assets
claims.supporting_quote: For instance, when quoting level 1 securities, while some managers may use the price on their favored cryptocurrency exchange, others might take an aggregate the price from multiple exchanges.7

claims.claim: The absence of digital asset valuation standards generates uncertainty and confusion for both investors and managers, and the industry would be better off with uniform standards.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
claims.supporting_quote: The lack of standards for digital asset valuation leads to uncertainty and confusion among investors and managers. The industry would benefit from uniform standards for digital asset valuation.

claims.claim: Arbitrage trading emerges in crypto markets because of information asymmetries across exchanges, which arise from imperfect disclosure, and the resulting decline in market efficiency is a key indicator of an inefficient market.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: multiple exchanges trading the same asset
claims.supporting_quote: The reason arbitrage trading starts to happen is because of asymmetries of information across the different exchanges. These asymmetries can happen as a result of imperfect disclosures or incite on whether a company has a willingness to take on debt.

claims.claim: Cross exchange price gaps in crypto do not self correct because of frictions on the arbitrageur side: South Korean investors faced foreign exchange conversion costs and regulatory capital controls that made exploiting the Bithumb premium impractical.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: South Korean investors seeking access to US exchanges
capital controls and foreign exchange frictions in place
claims.supporting_quote: It is unlikely any South Korean investor was able to take advantage of this opportunity because of the hurdles they would have to go through before being able to access the US exchange Coinbase.

claims.claim: Digital asset fund valuation disputes are aggravated by nondisclosure: Polychain Capital told a redeeming investor that the fund's asset valuation policy would not be disclosed.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: private digital asset funds
Polychain Capital redemption dispute
claims.supporting_quote: Upon request, Polychain Capital told Greenhouse the fund's asset valuation policy would not be disclosed.16

claims.claim: An investor who has been fully redeemed loses the ability to test the fund's valuation of his interest: the court held that Greenhouse retained no equity interest and therefore had no right to inspect the partnership's books and records.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: Delaware limited partnerships under 6 Del. C. section 17-305
investor has already withdrawn and been redeemed
claims.supporting_quote: Therefore, the court concluded that Greenhouse did not retain and equity interest in the partnership and was not entitled to inspect the partnership's books and records.25

claims.claim: Redemption contracts, the traditional price commitment device for privately issued money, lack credibility, whereas pre programmed smart contracts deliver an enforceable and secure quantity commitment instead.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: issuers of privately issued money
claims.supporting_quote: Such redemption contracts lack credibility.31 In contrast, the pre-programmed smart contract's enabled by cryptocurrencies facilitate an enforceable and secure quantity commitment.32

claims.claim: A programmed and enforceable quantity commitment secures a reliably positive value for Bitcoin because the governing source code is fully transparent on the blockchain and continuously verifiable.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: cryptocurrencies with observable open source code
claims.supporting_quote: For instance, a programmed enforceable quantity commitment ensures a reliable positive value of Bitcoin.33 Cryptocurrencies' observable source code are fully transparent on their respective blockchain and continuously verifiable.34

claims.claim: As of 2022 there is no agreed upon reliable valuation method for cryptocurrencies.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: as of 2022
claims.supporting_quote: An agreed-upon reliable valuation method does not exist for cryptocurrencies in 2022.

claims.claim: Fair market value is the legal standard for valuation, but it carries real world problems that limit its usefulness in practice.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
claims.supporting_quote: Fair market value is the legal standard for valuation, but it has real-world problems.48

claims.claim: Stocks and cryptocurrencies look similar enough, both traded on markets at fluctuating prices, to invite similar regulation, but they diverge in their potential for abuse, their nature, their acceptance, and their use.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: comparison of listed equities and cryptocurrencies
claims.supporting_quote: Stocks and cryptocurrencies are both traded on markets, with fluctuating prices, and seem similar enough in context to warrant similar regulation, yet they differ in their potential for abuse, their nature, acceptance, and use.64

claims.claim: The adjusted net asset approach revalues balance sheet items toward current fair value but still fails to capture intangible assets, because intangibles are not represented on the balance sheet.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: asset approach valuations relying on book values
claims.supporting_quote: However, the approach still fails to take into consider any intangible assets because they are not represented on the balance sheet.68

claims.claim: DCF currency translation breaks down for digital assets: no set discount rate or currency exchange forward curve exists for them, because they are not traded in exchange markets where closing prices are readily available and representative of fair value.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: DCF analysis where the projection currency is a digital asset rather than fiat
claims.supporting_quote: However, no such set discount rate or currency exchange forward curve is available for digital assets, as they are not traded in exchange markets where closing prices are readily available and representative of fair value.79

claims.claim: Principal to principal markets are generally not considered observable because little information about their transactions is publicly available, which pushes assets priced there out of the observable input levels.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: principal to principal markets
fair value input hierarchy
claims.supporting_quote: There is often little information about principal-to-principal transactions publicly available, and as such the markets are generally not considered observable.81

claims.claim: When the bid ask spread grows too wide while trades occur at high volume, the market begins to lose liquidity and the asset's value starts to fall, forcing investors who unload positions to surrender unrealized gains.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: exchange traded context
wide spreads combined with high trading volume
claims.supporting_quote: Historically, in an exchange context, if the spread between bid and ask price becomes too large and trades are occurring at high volumes, the market will start to lose liquidity and the value of the asset will start to fall.

claims.claim: Put option based discount models for lack of marketability have been widely used, but they can be inaccurate because real investors do not possess perfect market timing ability.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: prospective put model and related put option DLOM models
claims.supporting_quote: This model has been widely used by market participants to determine the discount on nonmarketable security. However, this method can be inaccurate because investors do not have perfect market-timing ability.102

claims.claim: The Longstaff model's assumptions are inconsistent with reality on two fronts: investors do not have perfect timing, and its assumed volatility of ten to thirty percent is far below the volatility exceeding fifty percent typical of small stocks.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: application of the Longstaff model to small or highly volatile securities
claims.supporting_quote: The Longstaff model's underlying assumptions are inconsistent with the reality of perfect timing as well as the assumed volatility level between ten to thirty percent, yet small stocks typically have volatility exceeding fifty percent.113

claims.claim: A major shortcoming of the QMDM is that no court in any case has accepted it, although it has been mentioned explicitly in three tax cases decided in 2000, 2001, and 2006.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: judicial acceptance in United States tax litigation
claims.supporting_quote: One major shortcoming of the QMDM is that it has not been accepted by any court in any case, but has been mentioned explicitly in three tax cases from 2000, 2001, and 2006.119

claims.claim: The main obstacle to digital asset market liquidity may be that the number of token holders has not continued to expand exponentially year over year; a larger stakeholder base would deepen liquidity and permit seamless entry and exit.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: centralized digital asset exchange markets
claims.supporting_quote: The main issue may be that the number of token holders have not continued to expand exponentially year over year. Having a greater number of stake holders may result in the deeper liquidity in the market, which would in turn allow for seamless movement in and out of the market.

claims.claim: Digital assets become less liquid precisely when large amounts are moved at once, because a large sell order floods the exchange and drives the price down.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: large block sales through a single exchange
claims.supporting_quote: Digital assets are less liquid when individuals try to move large amounts at once. If an individual wants to sell a large number of tokens through an exchange, they have to ensure they do not flood the market with token, causing price to drop on the exchange.

claims.claim: One design remedy for thin trading volume is supervision of digital asset exchanges by a federal governing authority or a self regulatory organization to assure compliance with existing laws.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: digital asset exchanges operating under legal uncertainty
claims.supporting_quote: To increase the trading volume, one solution may be to have a federal governing authority or a self-regulatory organization monitor the exchange to assure compliance with existing laws.

claims.claim: Legal uncertainty about crypto exchanges exerts a chilling effect on the market, and increased liquidity may follow once the market gains greater clarity on the legal issues surrounding this asset class.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: resolution of broker dealer status and securities law classification questions
claims.supporting_quote: Once the market gains greater clarity on the legal issues surrounding this new asset class, increased liquidity in the market may follow.

claims.claim: Market liquidity in digital assets is not only about exchanging crypto for fiat: allowing crypto to be used as a means of transacting for any good or service may itself increase market liquidity.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: buy in from the business community
claims.supporting_quote: Increasing liquidity does not mean only being able to exchange crypto for fiat currency, but also the ability to exchange for any good or service. By allowing for transactions to use crypto as a means of transaction may increase market liquidity.

claims.claim: Because digital asset exchanges perform both the traditional broker dealer function and the custody function, they face uncertainties and increased liability that traditional exchanges, which never touch custody, do not bear.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: centralized digital asset exchanges holding customer assets
claims.supporting_quote: By having the crypto exchange perform the services of a traditional broker/dealer and custody holder, digital asset exchanges face uncertainties and increased liability that do not impact traditional exchanges.124

claims.claim: When exchanges apply different standards about who may trade on their platform, the market ends up showing different prices for the same asset across exchanges, which is one reason trading arbitrage has become common in crypto.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: exchanges excluding participants by residence or other status
claims.supporting_quote: When different exchanges apply different standards as to who can trade on their platform, the market sees different prices for the same asset across exchanges.

claims.claim: The stablecoin exists as a response to digital asset price volatility: it is pegged to the value of an external asset, frequently a fiat currency.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: stablecoins pegged to external assets
claims.supporting_quote: To reduce price volatility in digital assets, the stablecoin was born. A stablecoin is pegged to the value of an external asset (frequently fiat currency).126

claims.claim: Digital assets resemble high growth companies for valuation purposes, so scenario planning is essential and business leaders must reason backward from the future rather than forward from the present, because the relevant markets may not yet exist.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: assets whose markets have not yet formed
claims.supporting_quote: Digital assets are comparable to high-growth companies, where scenario planning is critical because markets may not yet exist.129 In such a case, business leaders must start from the future rather than the present.

claims.claim: Secondary trade pricing from exchanges is a legitimate market approach input for digital assets only when liquidity is high enough to rely on those prices; where liquidity is lacking or unreliable, a discount for lack of liquidity is required.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: market approach applied to tokens
liquidity and depth differ between token to token and token to fiat trades
claims.supporting_quote: Secondary trade pricing (as seen in exchanges) are relevant when liquidity is high enough to rely on these prices.131

claims.claim: DCF appears at first glance unsuited to digital asset valuation because valuation is framed as pricing a token at a point in time, but it becomes applicable where networks return cash flows to token holders or to those who contribute work.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: networks that distribute cash flows to token holders or workers
claims.supporting_quote: However, some digital asset networks do return cash flows to token holders or those who contribute work to the network. In such a case, DCF can shed light on the role of these structures in digital asset valuation.

claims.claim: Under a deflationary token issuance model, which caps the number of tokens ever issued, prices are expected to increase because of the fundamental scarcity of token supply.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: deflationary token models such as Bitcoin
claims.supporting_quote: With a deflationary method, prices are expected to increase due to fundamental scarcity of token supply.

claims.claim: As the cryptocurrency market matures, inflationary token models may become more popular, because they permit stability mechanisms and therefore more experimentation with volatility mitigation.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: continued maturation of the cryptocurrency market
claims.supporting_quote: Several indicia seem to suggest that as the cryptocurrency market matures, inflationary token models may continue to become more popular. Inflationary token models allow the use of stability mechanisms, which may allow more experimentation with volatility mitigation.

claims.claim: Bitcoin's issuance schedule and relative scarcity are not necessarily the only reasons for its rise in value, since thousands of copycats share the same issuance schedule without matching its demand.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: scarcity based valuation models such as stock to flow
claims.supporting_quote: However, BTC's issuance schedule and relative scarcity are not necessarily the only reasons for its rise in value.147

claims.claim: Uniform digital asset valuation standards can only evolve over time as the market evolves, because standard setting requires common core practices, and those practices are only slowly emerging.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Hayley Howe, Digital Asset Valuation (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4033886
scope_conditions: standard setting for digital asset valuation
claims.supporting_quote: Such standards can evolve over time as the market evolves. Standard setting requires common core practices what are slowly evolving.

claims.claim: Even after the ICO boom of 2017 and 2018, many digital asset projects and token launches are designed with the primary focus on benefiting the founding group, which often finds creative ways to cash out of the project after a successful run.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: post 2018 crypto market cycle
token launches designed around a founding group
claims.supporting_quote: many digital asset projects and token launches are designed with the primary focus on benefiting the founding group, which often finds creative ways to cash out of the project after a successful run.

claims.claim: A fair launch is a token distribution in which the launched token is held entirely by the community and founders and their affiliates participate only on equal terms as members of that community.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
claims.supporting_quote: In a fair launch the launched token is held entirely by the community and all founders and their affiliates are equally part of the community.

claims.claim: The foundation model for token issuance is a core form of centralized top-down governance, and most ICO projects were governed by a small group of individuals rather than by the community at large or a DAO.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: ICO era token issuance
claims.supporting_quote: The foundation model for token issuance is a core form of centralized top-down governance in the context of token offerings.

claims.claim: ICOs that allowed their token to trade before the underlying product existed, at least in beta, created significant risk for investors because the product might never go live and the token could lose its value entirely.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: token trading opens before a working or beta product exists
claims.supporting_quote: ICOs that allowed their token to trade before the underlying product was built, at least in a beta version, create significant risk factors for the investors as the product may not go live at all and the token may lose its value entirely.

claims.claim: Fair launch tokens outperformed centrally distributed projects during the late 2020 and early 2021 rally: the collective crypto average token launch gained 112.41% over 90 days while fair launch projects gained over 296%.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: digital asset market rally of late 2020 and early 2021
90 day window after launch
claims.supporting_quote: During the digital asset market rally in late 2020 and early 2021, the collective crypto average token launch over 90 days increased 112.41%, while Fair Launch projects gained over 296%.

claims.claim: Fair launches shift capital formation from venture capitalism toward altruistic capitalism, because a digital asset startup that can successfully raise capital through a fair launch becomes less reliant on venture capital.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: startup can successfully raise capital via fair launch
claims.supporting_quote: In essence, if a digital asset startup can successfully raise capital from a fair launch, the startup will be less inclined/reliant on venture capital.

claims.claim: Fair token launches offer equal opportunity for market participants to acquire tokens over longer periods of time at a comparatively equal price.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: token launch claiming the fair launch label
claims.supporting_quote: fair token launches offer equal opportunity for market participants to acquire tokens over longer periods of time at a comparatively equal price.

claims.claim: Price equality in a fair launch means that no insider group or person can purchase the token at a significant discount.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: token launch claiming the fair launch label
claims.supporting_quote: Additionally, price equality in fair launch means that no insider group or person can purchase the token at a significant discount.

claims.claim: The fairness of a launch can be measured by how many individuals have access to the token at launch, assessed through the number of wallets holding the asset combined with the active participation of the wallet owners.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: token functioning as a traditional medium of exchange
claims.supporting_quote: To determine the fairness of a launch for a traditional medium of exchange it is possible to consider the number of wallets holding the token asset. Moreover, it is possible to consider the combination of distribution of the asset in wallets plus the active participation of the wallet owner.

claims.claim: Under the fairness to the public definition, a fair token launch requires that the token was launched without a founding team, a foundation, or a founding dev team.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: strict fairness to the public definition of fair launch
claims.supporting_quote: Under this definition, a fair token launch requires that the token was launched without a founding team, foundation, or founding dev team.

claims.claim: Under the fairness to the public definition of fair launch, no early investor may hold a pre-allocation of project tokens or a pre-mining program, and any individual claim to a percentage of token supply before public sale falls outside the definition of fair launch.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: strict fairness to the public definition of fair launch
claims.supporting_quote: under this definition of fair launch, no early investors would be permitted with a pre-allocation of project tokens or with a pre-mining program.

claims.claim: Bitcoin is one of the best examples of a fair launch because there was no ICO, no founders reward, no pre-mine, and no block reward for dev teams.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
claims.supporting_quote: Bitcoin is one of the best examples of a fair launch because there was no ICO, founders' reward, pre- mine, or block reward for dev teams.

claims.claim: Small market cap launches at very cheap initial prices carry the potential for team and whale purchase abuses, which is why equitable treatment of the public requires significant project-controlled liquidity.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: small market capitalization
very low initial token price
claims.supporting_quote: Small market cap launches at very cheap initial prices bring with them the potential abuses of team and whale purchases.

claims.claim: The larger the market capitalization controlled by the DAO, the less likely it becomes that whales and insiders can purchase inexpensive tokens on the market.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: DAO governance over project liquidity
claims.supporting_quote: The larger the market capitalization that is controlled by the DAO, the less likely it becomes that whales and insiders can purchase inexpensive tokens on the market.

claims.claim: The rule that no tokens may be distributed to insiders such as team, founders, associated whales, core investors, advisors, and marketing teams before or after the token sale is the most important staple of fair launch doctrine and cannot be subject to exceptions; any exception should cost the project the fair token launch designation.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: projects claiming the fair token launch designation
claims.supporting_quote: This rule is perhaps the most important key staple of the fair launch doctrine and cannot be subject to exceptions. Any exceptions to this rule should result in the loss of the designation fair token launch.

claims.claim: Because the main mandate of a fair launch is equitable treatment of the public, fair launches typically involve a mandate to distribute any and all revenue and profits of the project to community investors.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: project operating under fair launch principles
claims.supporting_quote: Since the main mandate of the fair launch is equitable treatment of the public, fair launches typically involve a mandate to distribute any and all revenue and profits of the project to their community investors.

claims.claim: Open-source code combined with protocol fee flowback to users, as with the Uniswap V2 0.3% swap fee that is automatically distributed to liquidity providers, guarantees transparency, accountability, market confidence in the product, and associated protections for the community.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: protocol has a viable product that produces revenue
code is open source
claims.supporting_quote: Open-source code and protocol fee flowback to users guarantee transparency, accountability, market confidence in the products, and the associated protections for the community.

claims.claim: A carve-out for start-up expenses is economically unavoidable in most fair launches because it is not feasible to expect founders operating without funding to keep spending time and resources on the project without payback assurances.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: founders operate without outside funding
project cannot raise outside capital in a reasonable timeframe
claims.supporting_quote: As a matter of fact, it may not be feasible to get founders who operate without funding to keep spending time and resources on the project without payback assurances.

claims.claim: Because pre-public token allocations to cover start-up costs run against the majority view on fair launches, preserving the spirit of fair launch requires that such allocations be fully transparent, announced to the community, and open to a community audit of the books.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: project allocates tokens before the public launch to cover startup costs
claims.supporting_quote: However, in order to maintain the spirit of fair launch, such token allocations before the public launch should be fully transparent and announced to the community with a community audit of the books, as desired.

claims.claim: Without significant marketing a fair launch token is less likely to reach a diverse set of market participants, and projects reaching only a few hundred investors with small million dollar market caps are much more prone to abuse and manipulation.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: token launches with limited marketing reach
claims.supporting_quote: Without significant marketing of the project, it is less likely the token will reach a diverse set of market participants. Projects that only reach a few hundred investors and only small million-dollar market caps are much more prone to abuse and manipulation.

claims.claim: Equal opportunity access points for public marketing incentives cannot be guaranteed and require constant reevaluation, so the public marketing permission for any fair token launch should be restricted to a limited percentage of total token supply.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: fair launch project grants public marketing incentives
claims.supporting_quote: These equal opportunity access points cannot be guaranteed and the process is subject to constant reevaluation. The public marketing permission for any fair token launch should be restricted to a limited percentage of total token supply.

claims.claim: The more decentralized the governance of a fair launch protocol, the less likely the project will be seen as treating public users unfairly, which makes a decentralized autonomous organization design advisable for fair launch projects.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: governance design is transparent and decentralized
claims.supporting_quote: The more decentralized the governance of a fair launch protocol, the less likely the project will be seen as not treating the public users unfairly. In this context, it may be advisable for fair launch projects to be launched in a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) design.

claims.claim: If the DAO governing a fair launch is controlled by a handful of people in a foundation setting, decentralized governance metrics are less likely to take hold and the public is correspondingly less likely to benefit from decentralized community governance over the launch.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: DAO controlled by a small group in a foundation setting
claims.supporting_quote: controlled by a handful of people in a foundation setting, it is less likely that decentralized governance metrics take hold in the DAO. Accordingly, it is less likely that the public can benefit from the decentralized community governance over the fair launch.

claims.claim: DAO governance built on fungible governance tokens is disfavored and dangerous because governance rights can be bought on open exchanges, whereas non-fungible reputation governance assures the highest levels of decentralization.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: DAO governance rights are tradeable on open exchanges
claims.supporting_quote: DAO governance that revolves around fungible governance tokens is disfavored and dangerous in this context as governance rights can be bought on open exchanges. By contrast, non-fungible reputation governance of the DAO assures highest levels of decentralization.

claims.claim: Community DAO governance makes any form of rug pull much less likely, because rug pulls typically benefit only a few select individuals who retained control over the project code or liquidity.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: community DAO oversees project code and liquidity
claims.supporting_quote: Community DAO governance also makes any form of rug pulls much less likely as rug pulls typically only benefit a few select individuals who retained control over the project code or liquidity.

claims.claim: DAO governance over token launch wallets can assure that no single individual exercises rights over the token launch wallet and becomes a single point of failure or abuse.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: token launch wallet is governed by the DAO
claims.supporting_quote: DAO governance over token launch wallets can assure that no single individual exercises rights over the token launch wallet and becomes a single point of failure/abuse.

claims.claim: Founders may hold significant influence over DAO votes initially depending on the DAO design, but higher levels of governance decentralization mitigate these centralization effects quickly through the onboarding of new DAO members.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: early stage of DAO formation
DAO design permits ongoing member onboarding
claims.supporting_quote: Depending on the DAO design, the founders may have significant influence over the DAO votes initially. However, higher levels of DAO governance decentralization mitigate these centralization effects quickly via the onboarding of new DAO members.

claims.claim: Whale purchases that soak up token supply at the earliest possible time in a launch are the key problem fair launch platforms address, because they can be the origin of significant centralization that harms the project for the entirety of its active market engagement.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: whales able to buy large amounts at the earliest moment of a launch
claims.supporting_quote: of whale token purchases that soak up supply at the earliest possible time in the token launch. Such whale purchases can be the origin of significant centralization of a token launch that may harm the project for the entirely of its active market engagement.

claims.claim: Technology platforms can make launch abuses less likely by mandating fair auctions in which tokens are released only in tranches, offering a limited number of tokens for a limited number of days, which makes rug pulls overall less likely.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: fair launch platform mandates auction format with tranche release
claims.supporting_quote: During such fair auctions, the tokens that are listed on the fair launch platforms may only be released in tranches, which makes rug pulls overall less likely. Such token tranche listings may offer a limited number of tokens for a limited number of days.

claims.claim: After half of each auction tranche is deposited into an AMM pair, the other half is allocated to open market purchasers and the remaining liquidity on the AMM is burned to ensure that any incentives for rug pulls are removed.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: auction based fair launch platform
Uniswap V2 compatible AMM
claims.supporting_quote: Thereafter, the other half of the tokens from the respective tranche may be allocated to open market purchasers. The remaining liquidity on the AMM may be burned to ensure that any incentives for rug pulls are removed.

claims.claim: Grin avoided privileging miners who could develop ASICs before launch by gradually scaling up the portion of coins allocated to the ASIC-friendly algorithm over two years, which allowed hobbyist miners to participate.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: dual proof of work offered over the first two years
claims.supporting_quote: However, Grin did not privilege miners who could develop ASICs prior to launch, rather they gradually scaled up the portion of coins allocated to the ASIC-friendly algorithm over 2 years, allowing hobbyist miners to participate.

claims.claim: Liquidity mining, one of the dominant mechanisms used for fair launches, undermines fairness because it leads those who already have more liquidity or assets to benefit disproportionally from the protocol.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: fair launch distributes rewards through liquidity mining
claims.supporting_quote: However, liquidity mining leads those who have more liquidity/assets to disproportionally benefit from the fair launch liquidity mining protocol.

claims.claim: If the top 10 addresses own a disproportionally large supply of a token, the project or community becomes more centralized, an outcome fair launches seek to avoid.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: token supply concentration measured across top holder addresses
claims.supporting_quote: If the top 10 addresses own a disproportionally large supply of a token, then the project or community becomes more centralized; an outcome which fair launches seek to avoid.

claims.claim: Binance implemented a subscription mechanism that gives everyone an equal opportunity to purchase newly released NFTs, responding to drops that sell out in seconds and leave interested users waiting for initial owners to flip.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: limited supply and high demand NFT drops
claims.supporting_quote: In response, Binance implemented a subscription mechanism that lets everyone have an equal opportunity to purchase newly released NFTs on its marketplace.

claims.claim: An auction mechanism for fair launch tokens avoids pricing tokens below their underlying market value, which in turn helps remedy the problems that derive from large whale token holders who can later manipulate the market.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: public auction of tokens at launch
claims.supporting_quote: An auction mechanism for fair launch tokens ensures avoids that tokens are priced cheaper than the underlying market value of the token. This, in turn, helps remedy the problems that derive from large whales token holders that can manipulate the market in the

claims.claim: No more than 40% of total token supply should be auctioned in a fair launch, with 10% serving as a buffer paired with raised funds as permanently locked DEX liquidity and the other 50% allocated to a DEX pair with the raise proceeds to provide long-term locked liquidity.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: public auction of tokens in a fair launch context
claims.supporting_quote: it is ill advised to auction more than 40% of the total token supply. 10% of token supply should serve as a buffer. paired with the funds raised to form permanently locked liquidity on a DEX. The other 50% should be allocated to a DEX in a pair with the funds from the token raise.

claims.claim: In a lottery fair launch protocol, a user who bids low for a ticket increases the potential secondary market return but decreases the chance of winning the lottery, because more users can afford to participate at a low price.
